hero.subtitle: When a death in Tehama was caused by someone else's carelessness, the family left behind has the right to ask hard questions. Our team works with Tehama County families on wrongful death claims at no upfront cost.

about.title: Tehama Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Tehama is a small town, and a sudden loss here is felt by nearly everyone. Public records for 2025 show 4 injury collisions and no traffic deaths in the city itself, but families in this part of Tehama County still lose loved ones on the roads that run through and around it. Collision counts are highest along State Route 36, State Route 32, and South Avenue, and reported crashes cluster on Fridays between midnight and 2 a.m. A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action, entirely separate from any criminal case, and it belongs to specific people: the spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Two years from the date of death is the general deadline, and it is shorter when a government entity is involved. We handle wrongful death cases directly on a contingency basis.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out who has the right to bring the claim in your family.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death, but the window shrinks considerably when a public agency, such as a county road department, may share responsibility. Acting promptly protects those rights.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, so grieving families are not asked to pay upfront. You only pay if we recover compensation for your family.

items.question: My relative died in a crash on State Route 36 near Tehama. Does a wrongful death case depend on criminal charges?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves forward independently of any criminal case the district attorney may or may not pursue. Even if no charges are filed, your family may still have a civil claim based on negligence. We can review the collision report and explain how the two processes differ.

items.question: What can a family actually recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs and the financial support the person would reasonably have provided over their lifetime. California also recognizes the loss of love, companionship, comfort, and guidance. The specific value depends on the facts of your family's situation, and no outcome can be promised.

items.question: How long do we have to act in Tehama County?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death, not the date of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency may be at fault, a claim usually has to be presented much sooner, often within six months. Because of that shorter window, it helps to speak with us early even if you are not ready to make decisions.
